evidence.quote: Presently, Strychnos spinosa can be propagated via seeds, grafting, or budding, with the production of fruit starting 3–5 years after planting
evidence.doc: Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: The review attributes this 3–5-year age to Avakoudjo et al.'s study in Benin, West Africa, rather than a South African bearing trial. Propagation method and local conditions must be confirmed before using it at a South African site; it is not a locally validated age or a yield-by-age curve.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Not found in any fetched source.

evidence.quote: Fruit weighs between 145 and 383 g, while about 300–700 fruits (40–100 kg) can be produced per tree stand.
evidence.doc: Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: The review reports 40–100 kg per tree stand without an annual period, mature age, matched cultivar or South African field conditions. Retain the original per-plant weight as context only: do not relabel it kg/year, spread it across months or treat it as a farm forecast.

chillUnits.notes: No source states a chilling requirement or explicitly says the species has none.

pollination.notes: SANBI states only 'It is believed that various insects pollinate the flowers.' (Ecology section, https://pza.sanbi.org/strychnos-spinosa) -- this confirms insect pollination but does not state whether the species is self-fertile, partly-self-fertile, needs a cross-pollinator, or is dioecious, so no enum value could be confidently assigned. The ICRAF Agroforestree Database 4.0 fact sheet for this species (fetched PDF) contains a BOTANIC DESCRIPTION, ECOLOGY, PRODUCTS, TREE MANAGEMENT and GERMPLASM MANAGEMENT section but NO BIOLOGY section with reproductive/phenology detail, unlike the fact sheets for other species in this batch.

supplementaryReferences.title: Harvest interval with unverified South African geography
supplementaryReferences.quote: Strychnos spinosa is a seasonal fruit tree that is harvested between August and December
supplementaryReferences.doc: Omotayo & Aremu (2021), Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange, section 3
supplementaryReferences.note: The review states August–December but does not identify a locality for that interval. Related monkey-orange literature discusses this interval in Zimbabwe and more than one Strychnos species; it does not establish a South African spinosa picking calendar. The former South Africa (general) window is withheld. Record the farm's own ripe-pulp months; seeds and unripe pulp are not ordinary food.

supplementaryReferences.title: Geography of the review's bearing-age citation
supplementaryReferences.quote: A participatory rural appraisal study was undertaken across three climatic zones in Benin.
supplementaryReferences.doc: Avakoudjo et al. (2020), Local Knowledge, Uses, and Factors Determining the Use of Strychnos spinosa Organs in Benin (West Africa), abstract
supplementaryReferences.note: The 2021 review cites this Benin study for its 3–5-year bearing-age statement. The cited source's geography is West Africa, not a South African orchard. Retain the review's numeric statement with this condition; no local annual yield curve is supplied.

gaps: South African ripe-picking months remain unverified. The former August–December South Africa (general) window was withdrawn in the 11 October 2026 provenance audit because the review does not state a harvest locality; it remains contextual supplementary evidence.

The review's first-bearing age cites a Benin study; no local South African first-bearing trial is verified. Its per-plant weight has no stated annual period or mature age, so no annual production schedule is inferred.
yearsToFullBearing: not found in any fetched source.
Precise pollination mechanism (self-fertile vs needing a cross-pollinator vs dioecious) not stated by any source found; only 'insects pollinate the flowers' (SANBI) is confirmed.
chillUnits: not stated by any source found.

The ICRAF Agroforestree Database PDF fact sheet for this species, unusually, has no BIOLOGY section (phenology/pollination content that exists for the other ICRAF fact sheets used in this project is simply absent here), so it contributed no additional facts beyond botanic description/ecology/products already covered by SANBI.
